layer1_identification.workType: single triangular wedge cut from a round scone, studded with hand-chopped chocolate chunks
layer1_identification.broadClassification: baked-good prop / stylized low-poly game asset, variant of base scone.ts
layer1_identification.note: reference is itself a stylized clay-render (AI generated), not a photograph - target look is soft matte clay, not photoreal. This is a variant object: silhouette/profile inherited by measurement from the base scone family, chip system is new.

layer2_form_silhouette.boundingVolume: thick triangular wedge (rounded-triangle footprint, three convex arcs meeting at three blunt corners), resting flat on its wide bottom face
layer2_form_silhouette.symmetry: asymmetric (hand-cut wedge, no exact mirror), one corner (apex) points toward camera-front
layer2_form_silhouette.shapeLanguage: organic form (soft rounded wedge, no sharp edges) with faceted chocolate inclusions (hard angular blocks) as contrast

measurements_topdown.footprint: rounded triangle, apex-front, two rounded rear lobes forming the back arc
measurements_topdown.heightOverWidth: roughly 0.46-0.47 (chunky, sturdy slice; never balanced on point, never upright) per assets/prompts/breads/scone--choco-chip.json geometry.silhouette

macro: wedge body (revolved/lofted shell: bottom face, side/cut faces, top crust)
meso: side crumb faces (plain cream, no chips)
micro: individual chocolate chunk (own facets, size, tilt)
1-2 soft crack fissures on top face

layer4_spatial: <top crust face, above, side crumb faces> contact: shared rim edge, hard material-boundary crease (2-tone crust split)
<chocolate chunks, embedded-in, top crust face> contact: embed - each chunk sits half-sunken, dough visibly hugging its base edge, not resting on top like a bump
<fissures, recessed-into, top crust face> contact: shallow concave crease, does not cross onto side faces
no floating parts; wedge rests on its own flat bottom face

surfaces.relief: smooth clay with 1-2 shallow crack fissures + fine crumb ridging near rim
smooth clay, fine vertical crumb ridging, completely plain (no chips)
hard flat facets - deliberately different shading language from the soft dough (hard inclusion vs soft matrix)

layer5_materials.runtimeNote: consumer runtime force-replaces every material with MeshLambertMaterial keeping only map+color (scripts/breads/types.ts section 2); PBR scalars beyond albedo are inert

layer6_color.source: assets/prompts/breads/scone--choco-chip.json geometry.crust (authoritative, hand-transcribed) - JSON is color/ratio canon, image is form/proportion canon only (docs/BREADS.md decision)
layer6_color.observedVsSpec: reference top-down crust reads slightly darker (~222) than the 3/4 view (~238) due to camera-angle-dependent AO in the AI render; JSON hex is used as flat albedo per CRIB measurement-fixture rule (top-down as reference plane)

layer7_identity_features: rounded-triangle wedge silhouette, apex-front, height ~ 0.47x width - identity-critical, must not read as a cone/cylinder or stand upright
hard 2-tone crust split at the rim (golden top vs plain cream sides) - identity-critical material boundary
1-2 soft crack fissures on the top crust, not more

about 7 solid chocolate chunks, hand-chopped: each has its own facet count/size/tilt (no two identical), size hierarchy (2 large, ~4 medium, 1 small shard) reads clearly, gathered in loose casual clusters leaving quiet plain crust between them, NOT a uniform grid and NOT evenly spaced studs
chunks sit half-sunken into the crust (dough hugs the base edge) - never a bump sitting on top, never a spike growing out of the surface
side/cut faces stay completely plain - no chunks visible on the cut faces (identity-critical negative: earlier round's edge-chip system was rejected by user for reading as a mechanical row of dots)
layer8_uncertainty: underside is never visible (rests flat on display) - modelled as a closed low-detail cap

exact chunk placement is not identity-critical; count (~7), size hierarchy, hand-chopped facet irregularity, half-sunken embed and loose clustering ARE identity-critical and are procedurally seeded from the builder rng

front-elevation reference (scone--choco-chip-2.png) is a known generation error (renders as a slab, not a wedge) and is excluded as a shape reference per assets/breads/work/CRIB.md; only its height/width ratio is usable
reference renders carry soft AI-generated ambient occlusion in the chunk crevices that the flat-lit breadlab harness will not reproduce identically; expected delta, not a defect
